panels.title: Successful S3 LIST requests - $bucket (last 1h)
panels.description: Successful LIST requests for the selected buckets. Bucket names come from metric labels and support per-site and custom names. Requests can come from any S3 client, so this is activity, not proof that the edge uploader is healthy. Prometheus increase can return fractional estimates.

panels.title: Volume data-file bytes (all collections)
panels.description: Sum of the normal volume-size gauge across all collections. The deleted_bytes gauge describes deleted content already included in normal bytes, so adding it would double-count. This excludes filesystem overhead, indexes, and filer storage; total filesystem capacity needs separate disk telemetry, which may not be installed.

panels.title: S3 requests/min - $bucket (last 5m)
panels.description: Rolling 5-minute average request rate for the selected buckets, scaled to per-minute. Request counts do not measure DICOM delivery.

panels.title: Volumes (across all buckets)
panels.description: Maximum reported volume count for the current single-volume-server deployment. Collection label series repeat the server total, so summing them would overcount. This is an allocated volume count, not used bytes or a capacity guarantee.

panels.title: S3 request rate by HTTP code - $bucket
panels.description: Per-second request rate for the selected buckets, grouped by HTTP response code. Inspect 4xx/5xx responses for client or server failures.

panels.title: S3 request rate by operation type - $bucket
panels.description: Per-second S3 request rate for the selected buckets, grouped by operation. Multipart requests and retries are not one-to-one with files; this is not a DICOM count.

panels.title: SeaweedFS log tail
panels.description: Management SeaweedFS logs selected by the pod app label, independent of the Helm release namespace. The bucket dropdown does not filter these service logs.
